node:topic:24ac1bf579.title: Stateless HMAC-SHA256 Session Tokens
node:topic:24ac1bf579.summary:
- Purpose
  - Replace plaintext session cookies with tamper-evident, stateless tokens to simplify auth and reduce server-side state.
- Design and Implementation
  - Custom token format: base64url-encoded JSON payload + "." + hex HMAC-SHA256 signature.
  - Sign/verify helpers use constant-time compare for signatures.
  - Secrets sourced from environment variables (per PR description).
- Key Trade-offs
  - Integrity without confidentiality: payload is readable; avoid sensitive data in token body.
  - Simpler than JWT (no headers/claims/deps), but lacks standardized claims (exp/iat), kid, and built-in rotation metadata.
  - Requires disciplined key management and rotation strategy.
- PRs and Issues
  - PR #101: Add HMAC-SHA256 token signing to auth module; replaces plaintext cookie; env-based keys. Reviewer: “LGTM, please add a rotation test.”
  - Issue #201: Enable key rotation without invalidating live sessions via dual-key verification during a rotation window; proposal to use keys.previous env var.
- Next Steps
  - Implement dual-key verify (accept current and previous; sign with current only) and add rotation tests.
  - Consider adding exp/iat and optional kid to ease rotation and session expiry.
  - Validate env var loading, key entropy/length, and operational rotation procedure.

node:topic:47ebd60850.title: Session Expiration and Refresh Mechanism
node:topic:47ebd60850.summary:
- Purpose
  - Introduce clear session expiry semantics and a server-side refresh flow to renew valid sessions without re-authentication.
- Key changes
  - Session model adds is_expired(now) to determine validity via a simple time comparison (now >= expires_at).
  - New refresh endpoint (per PR description) to exchange an expiring/expired session for a refreshed one.
- Design decisions and trade-offs
  - Pure function signature for expiry check (caller supplies now), improving testability and eliminating hidden time dependencies; trade-off is slightly more caller responsibility.
  - Boundary defined as inclusive expiry (equal to expires_at counts as expired), minimizing ambiguity at cutoff times.
  - Keeps expiration logic minimal and centralized in the Session class, reducing duplication across endpoints.
- PRs represented
  - PR #102: Adds is_expired and introduces a refresh endpoint; diff explicitly shows the is_expired addition, with server route changes implied.
- Impact and considerations
  - Clarifies and standardizes session lifecycle handling across the codebase.
  - Security: tighter control over stale sessions; refresh flow can enforce policies (e.g., max lifetime) if extended.
  - Backward compatibility: additive change with low risk; callers must adopt the new check before invoking refresh logic.

node:topic:dfe0c6ec47.title: Lightweight Templating Evolution
node:topic:dfe0c6ec47.summary:
- Purpose: Introduce a minimal {{var}} templating renderer and quickly harden it for safe HTML output.
- PR #103: Added a simple renderer that replaces {{key}} with str(ctx[key]) via straightforward string substitution. Chose minimalism to ship fast; acknowledged lack of escaping.
- PR #104: Escapes context values with html.escape before substitution to mitigate XSS. Opted for default-escaped output (secure-by-default) over configurability.
- Issue #202: Renderer treats {{user.name}} literally; no dotted-path resolution. Comment notes it was fixed in PR #109 (not shown here).
- Design decisions/trade-offs:
  - Simplicity over full templating semantics (no parser, filters, or conditionals).
  - String replacement loop is order-dependent and can re-render placeholders that appear in inserted values.
  - Universal HTML escaping may not suit non-HTML targets; escaping is not configurable per key/context.
  - Type handling via str(v); potential need to ensure escape happens after string conversion.
- Likely next steps: dotted-path resolution, tokenization to avoid cascading replacements, configurable/opt-out escaping, and broader template features.

node:topic:c8636bb50e.title: HTTP Router and Middleware Evolution
node:topic:c8636bb50e.summary:
- Purpose
  - Introduce a minimal HTTP router that dispatches requests by (method, path), then evolve it with default 404 handling and a middleware pipeline.
- Core design
  - Routes stored in a dict keyed by (method, path) → handler for O(1) exact-match dispatch.
  - Initial behavior raised KeyError on missing routes; later replaced with a default 404 handler to normalize error handling.
  - Middleware introduced via a middleware() decorator, enabling composition around handlers.
- Evolution
  - PR #105: Basic router with add(method, path, handler) and dispatch(method, path, req).
  - PR #106: Adds default 404 handler and a middleware chain/decorator.
- Trade-offs
  - Simplicity and speed of exact-match routing vs. lack of parameterized paths.
  - Exception on missing route vs. predictable HTTP 404 response.
  - Middleware flexibility requires deterministic ordering; data structure choice impacts this.
- Quality and correctness
  - Comment (@eve): Add tests to assert middleware ordering.
  - Issue #203: Middleware order is non-deterministic when using sets; must preserve registration order (prefer list/insertion-ordered structures) and test it.
- Outcome
  - A small, extensible router foundation with a clearer error path and middleware hooks; next step is fixing and validating deterministic middleware ordering.

node:topic:0bfca44a5b.title: Minimal In-Memory Model Storage
node:topic:0bfca44a5b.summary:
- Purpose: Provide a tiny, dependency-free, in-memory persistence layer for prototyping/tests by storing model instances as dicts.
- Core design:
  - Base Model holds a class-level _rows list.
  - save() appends the instance’s __dict__ to storage.
  - all() returns a shallow-copied list of stored rows.
- Notable design inconsistency/bug:
  - save() writes to Model._rows (hard-coded), while all() reads cls._rows. Subclasses may read different storage than they write to, causing cross-model contamination or “missing” records.
- Trade-offs:
  - Extremely simple and fast, no setup or external dependencies.
  - Sacrifices isolation (shared storage), safety, and fidelity (stores dicts, not instances).
  - Mutable reference leak: stored dicts reflect later instance mutations (no snapshot).
  - No IDs, querying, validation, or thread-safety; only ephemeral process memory.
- Recommended next steps:
  - Use cls._rows in save() and define per-subclass storage.
  - Snapshot on save (e.g., dict(self.__dict__)).
  - Provide reset/clear utilities and basic querying.
  - Consider returning instances or a typed record wrapper.
  - Add tests for subclass isolation and mutation behavior.

node:topic:af105720b9.title: Evolving ORM: Save, Filter, SQLite
node:topic:af105720b9.summary:
- Goal: Bootstrapped a minimal ORM with a consistent Model API, then upgraded persistence from an in-memory store to SQLite for durability and richer querying.
- PR #107: Base Model.save()/all()
  - Introduces Model class with save() and all().
  - Uses a trivial in-memory row store to unblock development and tests.
  - Trade-off: simplicity and speed over durability and scalability; intended as a temporary backend.
- PR #108: filter(**kw) and SQLite backend
  - Adds Model.filter(**kw) for simple equality-based queries via keyword arguments.
  - Replaces in-memory storage with sqlite3, standardizing on a real database.
  - Trade-offs: Slightly higher complexity (connections/schema) for significant gains in persistence, query capabilities, and future scalability.
  - Maintains the minimal, Pythonic API (save/all/filter) while decoupling storage concerns.
- Known limitation (Issue #204): N+1 queries in Model.all()
  - Current all() issues one query per row, leading to poor performance.
  - Signals a need to batch retrieval (single SELECT) and possibly refine row-to-model hydration.
- Overall design choices:
  - Start simple, stabilize API, then swap backends.
  - Favor kwargs-based filters over a heavy query DSL to keep the learning curve low and implementation lean.

node:subsystem:0078c365f2.title: Stateless HMAC Sessions With Refresh
node:subsystem:0078c365f2.summary:
- Objective
  - Replace plaintext cookies with stateless, tamper-evident HMAC-SHA256 tokens; define explicit expiry semantics and a refresh flow.
- Design overview
  - Token: base64url-encoded JSON payload + "." + hex HMAC-SHA256 signature; constant-time signature compare; secrets from environment.
  - Session lifecycle: Session.is_expired(now) with inclusive cutoff; refresh endpoint to renew valid/near-expiry sessions without re-auth.
- Key decisions and trade-offs
  - Integrity without confidentiality: payload readable; avoid sensitive fields.
  - Simpler than JWT (no headers/claims/deps), but lacks exp/iat, kid, rotation metadata.
  - Statelessness reduces server state, shifting complexity to key management/rotation and disciplined expiry handling.
  - Pure time injection (caller supplies now) improves testability at minor caller overhead.
- PRs and issues
  - PR #101: Add HMAC signing/verification; replace plaintext cookie; env-based keys. Reviewer asked for rotation test.
  - Issue #201: Dual-key verification during rotation window via keys.previous env var.
  - PR #102: Add is_expired(now) and a refresh endpoint; centralize and standardize expiry semantics.
- Impact
  - Clear, consistent session lifecycle; tighter control over stale sessions; groundwork for policy enforcement (e.g., max lifetime).
  - Backward-compatible; callers must adopt is_expired before refresh.
- Next steps
  - Implement dual-key verify (accept previous, sign with current) and add tests.
  - Consider exp/iat and optional kid to ease rotation and expiry.
  - Validate env var loading, key entropy/length, and rotation procedures.

node:subsystem:365e993932.title: Minimal Templating and Router Hardening
node:subsystem:365e993932.summary:
- Scope: Ship tiny building blocks fast (templating, routing), then harden for safety and predictable behavior.
- Lightweight templating
  - PR #103: Introduced minimal {{key}} substitution via str(ctx[key]); no escaping to prioritize speed to ship.
  - PR #104: Added html.escape on values (after str()) for secure-by-default HTML output; chose simplicity over per-key configurability.
  - Known gaps: No dotted-paths (Issue #202; later noted fixed in PR #109), order-dependent replacement can cascade/re-render placeholders, no parser/filters/conditionals, escaping not target-aware (HTML-only).
  - Trade-offs: Extreme simplicity and few deps vs. limited semantics and potential replacement hazards. Next: dotted paths, tokenization to prevent cascading, configurable/opt-out escaping.
- HTTP router and middleware
  - PR #105: Exact-match router using dict[(method, path)] -> handler for O(1) dispatch.
  - PR #106: Replaced KeyError with default 404; added middleware() decorator to compose handler wrappers.
  - Trade-offs: Speed and simplicity vs. no parameterized paths; middleware requires deterministic registration order.
  - Quality: Comment (@eve) to test middleware ordering; Issue #203 flags non-determinism with sets—switch to insertion-ordered structures and add tests.
- Outcome: A small, extensible core for templating and routing, quickly secured and normalized; clear roadmap to determinism, configurability, and richer features.

node:subsystem:c6c2761425.title: From In-Memory to SQLite ORM
node:subsystem:c6c2761425.summary:
- Purpose: Bootstrap a tiny ORM for prototyping/tests, then harden it with a durable backend while preserving a minimal, Pythonic API.
- Initial in-memory storage:
  - Design: Base Model keeps class-level _rows; save() appends instance __dict__; all() returns a shallow copy.
  - Bug/inconsistency: save() writes to Model._rows while all() reads cls._rows → cross-model contamination or “missing” records in subclasses.
  - Trade-offs: dependency-free and fast, but shared storage, no IDs/querying/validation/thread-safety, and mutable reference leaks (no snapshot).
  - Suggested fixes: use cls._rows per subclass; snapshot dict(self.__dict__) on save; add clear/reset and simple querying; consider instance/typed wrappers; test subclass isolation and mutation behavior.
- Evolution and PRs:
  - PR #107: Introduces Model.save()/all() with in-memory backend to stabilize the API quickly.
  - PR #108: Adds filter(**kw) and swaps persistence to sqlite3, decoupling storage and enabling real queries.
- SQLite trade-offs: modest complexity (connections/schema) for durability, richer querying, and scalability; API remains save/all/filter.
- Known limitation: Issue #204 — Model.all() triggers N+1 queries; needs batched SELECT and improved hydration.
- Design approach: Start simple, lock the API, then replace the backend; favor kwargs-based filters over a heavy query DSL.

node:repo:7e5a351fcd.title: synth/webframework
node:repo:7e5a351fcd.summary:
- Program-wide arc: ship tiny primitives quickly, then harden for security, determinism, and durability while preserving minimal, Pythonic APIs and low dependencies.
- Stateless HMAC sessions
  - Replace plaintext cookies with base64url JSON + HMAC-SHA256 and constant-time verify; env-sourced secrets. Stateless lifecycle via is_expired(now) (inclusive) and a refresh endpoint. Integrity without confidentiality; simpler than JWT; caller-supplied time for testability. (PRs #101, #102; Issue #201)
  - Trade-offs: less server state vs. key rotation/expiry rigor. Impact: consistent renewals, tighter stale-session control; backward-compatible (callers adopt is_expired). Next: dual-key verify, exp/iat/kid, key validation.
- Minimal templating and router hardening
  - Templating: start with {{key}} -> str(); add html.escape for secure-by-default HTML. Known gaps: cascading replacements, no filters/conditionals; dotted paths added later. (PRs #103, #104, #109; Issue #202)
  - Router: exact-match dict[(method, path)] -> handler (O(1)); default 404; middleware decorator. Determinism concerns (ordering, sets) addressed by using insertion-ordered structures and tests. (PRs #105, #106; Issue #203; reviewer note on ordering)
  - Trade-offs: speed/simplicity over features (no param routes; explicit middleware order).
- ORM: in-memory to SQLite
  - Establish API with in-memory Model.save()/all(); found subclass storage bug and mutation leaks; propose per-subclass rows and snapshots. (PR #107)
  - Swap backend to sqlite3; add filter(**kw); retain simple API; note N+1 in all() to batch. (PR #108; Issue #204)
  - Trade-offs: modest complexity for durability and real queries; avoid heavy DSL, favor kwargs filters.
